result:
I captured all five cards from the real, unmodified production build, with nothing blocking. I opened the screenshots and each one shows the whole card. The rendered card text matches the app's own computed result for each card, word for word and number for number.

**Cards** (fixture IDs `s8a-v1-c1…c5`):

| Card | What it shows | Confidence label | Browser clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Pattern change | pattern change | Strong read | export end + 1 h |
| 2 Steady/balanced | balanced contact | Strong read | export end + 1 h |
| 3 Carried (mixed) | mixed contact | Useful read | export end + 1 h |
| 4 Unusual silence | current quiet longer than 10 of 10 earlier ones, with the restart-history note | Useful read | export end + 15 days |
| 5 Not enough data | not enough evidence | Light read | export end + 1 h |

- **Fixtures:** cards 1 and 5 use committed test fixtures unchanged. Cards 2–4 use the generators from `tests/relationship-read.ts`, copied byte-for-byte; every run checks the copy against the source, and regenerating gave identical hashes.
- **Capture setup:** en-US locale, UTC timezone, clock frozen before import, upload through the app's real file input.
- **Checks:** build, `npm test`, typecheck and parity tests all pass. The relationship-read tests pass. Product code is unchanged. The local server and browser are stopped.

**Problems you'll want to look at:**
1. **Card borders differ between cards.** A CSS ordering bug in the shipped app means cards 1 and 4 get a plain grey border instead of their colour accent. Cards 2 and 3 get a full purple outline instead of just a left stripe. Participants will see a different frame on the two contact cards. Fixing it means changing product code, so it would need a separate draft PR.
2. **The limitation line is hard to read.** It's light grey 11px text at 2.56:1 contrast, below the accessibility minimum of 4.5:1. That's the line saying the card can't explain why, so it may be the one people miss in a ten-second exposure.
3. **Desktop shows the app as a narrow phone frame.** The card is only 344px wide with 11–12px text. I added a 2× version of each card for high-resolution displays alongside the 1× one; which to show is your call.
4. **Mobile is fine:** every card fits on the first 390×844 screen with nothing cropped. The whole-page screenshots also show the app's existing "What to notice" summary below the card, which emphasises something different from the card itself on cards 1 and 4. The card-only images avoid that.
5. **Wording quirks, captured exactly as shown:**
   - Card 1 mixes "2026-04-01 to 2026-04-14" style dates with "May 7, 2026".
   - Card 3 has a clumsy "…and follow-ups before a reply and turn share stayed close to even".
   - Cards 2 and 3 say "Across 4 measures" but only list three.

**Not mine, but it will fail:** `npm run lint` errors out on your `preflight/validate-schema.cjs` (12 errors from `require` and `__dirname`). The app itself lints clean without that file.

**Commands run:** `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then `npm run build` (build ID `5gkiF1dwfx9VnG1NwZcVc`), then the three scripts with `TZ=UTC npx tsx`: `generate-fixtures.ts`, `capture.ts`, `write-manifest.ts`. The full command list is in the report.

**Receipt:** `manifest.json` sha256 `e498e0f10e8c32770f96628d076d9efdd193d16e6829fff54d8e46d08f4dde24`. The full provenance JSON (model `claude-opus-5-5`, native Claude Code CLI, base commit `2415a51…`) is at the end of the report.
